intro: The Ependymoma — Toronto Stage is a oncology scoring tool used in paediatric practice. Staged by the presence of metastatic disease. It scores 1 criteria and interprets the total across 2 bands, so the number always arrives with the severity it implies rather than on its own. In PediAid each criterion is shown as a labelled option with the weight it carries, so the total can be checked rather than taken on trust.
indications: Grading severity at the bedside in oncology
Recording an objective severity band in the case notes
Deciding when a total crosses the threshold for escalation
Re-scoring to track whether a child is improving or deteriorating
Checking the exact criteria of a score used infrequently
method: The score sums 1 criteria: Metastatic status at diagnosis. Totals are then banded: 1 stage or more - Stage I: localised ependymoma. Extent of resection is the strongest prognostic factor - aim for gross total resection followed by focal radiotherapy; 2 stage or more - Stage II: metastatic ependymoma - craniospinal radiotherapy and chemotherapy; significantly poorer prognosis.
guidelineRefs: Source: Gupta S, Aitken JF, Bartels U et al. Paediatric cancer stage in population-based cancer registries: the Toronto consensus principles and guidelines. Lancet Oncol 2016;17:e163-72.

faqs.q: How many criteria does the Ependymoma — Toronto Stage use?
faqs.a: 1. They are Metastatic status at diagnosis.

faqs.q: What do the bands of the Ependymoma — Toronto Stage mean?
faqs.a: The total is interpreted as: 1 stage or more - Stage I: localised ependymoma. Extent of resection is the strongest prognostic factor - aim for gross total resection followed by focal radiotherapy; 2 stage or more - Stage II: metastatic ependymoma - craniospinal radiotherapy and chemotherapy; significantly poorer prognosis.

faqs.q: Does the score replace clinical judgement?
faqs.a: No. It is a structured way to record and communicate severity. A clinician concerned about a child should act on that concern regardless of the total.

faqs.q: Where does this score come from?
faqs.a: Source: Gupta S, Aitken JF, Bartels U et al. Paediatric cancer stage in population-based cancer registries: the Toronto consensus principles and guidelines. Lancet Oncol 2016;17:e163-72.
